blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Most countries now have laws that protect personal data. In Europe, the most famous is GDPR. In Brazil, it is LGPD. The rules are different in detail, but they share a simple idea: companies must respect the privacy of the people whose data they hold.

In practice, a company has to know exactly what personal data it has, why it has it, who can see it, and how long it keeps it. It has to ask for consent when consent is needed. And it has to delete data when it is no longer needed.

Data protection is not paperwork. It is a promise to the people who trusted you with their information. Breaking that promise — even by accident — is one of the fastest ways to lose customer trust.

items.q: What is the famous data law in Europe?
items.why: "In Europe, the most famous is GDPR."

items.q: What simple idea do the rules share?
items.why: "companies must respect the privacy of the people whose data they hold."

items.q: When must a company delete data?
options: When it is no longer needed
items.why: "it has to delete data when it is no longer needed."

items.q: The author would most likely DISAGREE with the idea that…
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz "Data protection is not paperwork" — o autor discorda dessa ideia.

items.q: The last paragraph suggests that losing customer trust…
options: is easy and can happen fast
items.why: Inferência: "even by accident — is one of the fastest ways to lose customer trust" mostra que a confiança se perde fácil e rápido.

blocks.instruction: Ouça Charlotte falando com uma nova colega. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Hi, welcome to the team! Let me show you how we think about data here. It is quite simple. For every set of data we hold, we ask four questions.

First: what? What personal data do we have? Names, emails, phone numbers. We must always know exactly what we are keeping.

Second: why? Why do we have this data? There must be a good reason. If there is no reason, we should not keep it.

Third: who? Who can see this data? Not everyone. Only the people who really need it for their work. This keeps the data safe.

And fourth: how long? How long do we keep it? When we do not need the data any more, we have to delete it. We cannot keep it forever.

These four questions — what, why, who, and how long — protect our clients. They trust us with their information, and that trust is very important. So please, if you are not sure about any dataset, come and ask me. It is always better to ask.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: How many questions does the team ask about each set of data?
items.why: "we ask four questions" — what, why, who, and how long.

items.q: Who can see the data, according to Charlotte?
options: Only people who really need it
items.why: "Only the people who really need it for their work."

items.q: What must the team do when they do not need the data any more?
items.why: "When we do not need the data any more, we have to delete it."

items.q: Charlotte suggests that the new colleague should…
options: ask her when they are not sure
keep all data just in case
items.why: Inferência: "if you are not sure... come and ask me. It is always better to ask."

items.q: Why does Charlotte think the four questions are important?
options: They protect the clients and their trust
They help the company sell data
They are required only in Europe
items.why: Inferência: "These four questions... protect our clients. They trust us... and that trust is very important."

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "Your name and email are personal data." Personal data is…
items.why: Personal data = dados pessoais: informação sobre uma pessoa.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "We must ask for ___ before we collect someone's data."
items.why: Consent = consentimento: a permissão da pessoa.

items.q: "When we do not need the file, we delete it." To delete means to…
items.why: To delete = apagar, remover.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "The client gave us their data, so we must not break their ___."
items.why: Trust = confiança: o que a pessoa deposita na empresa.

items.q: "We respect the privacy of our clients." To respect privacy means to…
options: keep their information safe and private
items.why: To respect privacy = respeitar a privacidade, manter os dados seguros e privados.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs comuns em reuniões sobre dados. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "The manager has to sign off on the new privacy rules." To sign off on means to…
items.why: Sign off on = aprovar, dar o aval.

items.q: "We will roll out the new data policy next month." To roll out means to…
items.why: Roll out = colocar em prática, começar a usar.

items.q: "Some staff pushed back on the new rules." They…
items.why: Push back on = resistir, discordar.

items.q: "We agreed to delete old files, but nobody followed through." They…
items.why: Follow through = levar a tarefa até o fim.

items.q: "If there is a data problem, we must speak up." To speak up means to…
options: say something and not stay quiet
items.why: Speak up = falar, dizer o que se pensa em vez de ficar calado.
